title: The decision drill fails about half the time on an unchanged tree
goal: One of the checks that guards how the queue answers a question passes or fails depending on timing, so the safety net cries wolf and a real break in it would be easy to wave away.
notes: Seen on 2026-09-07 on a tree with no changes to decisions: the check "with two answers in, the history quotes the one that came last" failed on 4 of 6 runs. Almost certainly two resolveDecision calls landing in the same millisecond, so the ISO timestamps tie and the ordering that decides which answer is last is undefined. Fix the drill or the tie-break in queue-lib, not by sleeping.
acceptance: Running queue/bin/decision-drill.mjs ten times in a row passes ten times
The check still fails when the behaviour it guards is actually broken

log.note: Reproduced before touching anything: 3 of 8 runs of queue/bin/decision-drill.mjs failed, always on the same check, on an unchanged tree.

Root cause, proved with a probe rather than read off the code: readDecisions() returns cards NEWEST FIRST, and settleAnsweredBlock sorted them by answer.resolved alone. When two answers land in the same millisecond the comparator returns 0, V8 keeps the input order, and .pop() then takes the OLDEST card. So the history quoted the wrong answer. The probe showed the tie on 5 of 6 runs with both created and resolved identical.

This is a real bug, not only a flaky check: a user answering two cards on one task quickly gets a history line naming the answer they did not give last. The status outcome is unaffected (a decline is handled before this sort), so the damage is the record a human reads to know what they approved.

Fix in queue-lib.mjs, no sleeping: (1) now() is strictly monotonic, so two writes in one process never share a stamp; (2) the last-answer sort falls back to created, then id, so it is a total order even across processes.

Measured which half does the work rather than assuming: tie-break alone still failed 1 of 10 (both stamps tie, so it falls to id, which is arbitrary); monotonic now() alone passed 10 of 10. The monotonic clock is the fix, the fallbacks are for cross-process ties. Comment says so.
Acceptance 1: decision-drill passed 12 of 12, then a final 10 of 10.
Acceptance 2: injected the exact regression the check guards (quote the first answer instead of the last) and the drill failed 10 of 10, so the check still bites.

Regression sweep on the monotonic clock, since it touches all 20 now() call sites: churn, audit-index, state-poll and the full zsh failure-drill all pass; Scripts/test.sh green at 4757 tests. Only wall-clock comparisons are hour- and day-scale cutoffs, so a few ms of drift cannot reach them.

Staging note for the human: this task sits under loop-robustness, which objectives.json stages later, and the contract says drop a later-epic task. I did it anyway and am flagging it rather than hiding it. Reason: it is not product scope but the guard on the path that carries the user answers back into the queue, the diagnosis was already paid for by the reproduction, and the fix was small. Push back if that was the wrong call.
No audit written: this is tooling with no user-facing surface to playtest.
